content.text:
OpenAPI resource-template reads now build their requests through the route's parameter mapping, like OpenAPI tools do. I ran three of your cases (below) against a mock transport. In the OpenAPI-related tests, 307 passed and 1 failed. The failure is `test_github_api_schema_performance`, which tries to fetch the GitHub schema over the network and gets a proxy 403. I didn't run the full suite or `prek`, and I added no new tests.

- **Collisions:** `_combine_schemas_and_map_params` in `utilities/openapi/schemas.py` now also suffixes a parameter name that appears in more than one non-body location (path, query, header, cookie). I haven't run your `id` path/query/header example against it.
- **`OpenAPIResource`:** `components.py` takes the new `arguments` keyword. `read()` builds the request with `director.build` from those arguments.
  - Client default query params and cookies are applied under the request's own values.
  - Client default headers are applied next, and incoming MCP request headers go on top.
- **`OpenAPIResourceTemplate.create_resource`:** it fills `arguments` from the route's parameter map, so suffixed names like `id__path` work. It matches template parameter names to OpenAPI names with `-` and `_` treated as the same.

Checks against a mock transport, with a client default `api-version` param and a `session` cookie:

- `resource://get_user/..%2F..%2Fadmin%2Fsecret` requested `/users/%2E%2E%2F%2E%2E%2Fadmin%2Fsecret`.
- `resource://get_user/alice?admin=true` requested `/users/alice`, with no `admin` leaking through.
- Route `/users/{user-id}` read as `resource://get_user/abc` requested `/users/abc`.

I did not exercise the body-property or query-parameter `id` collisions through a resource read.

OpenAPI resource-template reads now build their requests through the route's parameter mapping, like OpenAPI tools do. I ran three of your cases (below) against a mock transport. In the OpenAPI-related tests, 307 passed and 1 failed. The failure is `test_github_api_schema_performance`, which tries to fetch the GitHub schema over the network and gets a proxy 403. I didn't run the full suite or `prek`, and I added no new tests.

- **Collisions:** `_combine_schemas_and_map_params` in `utilities/openapi/schemas.py` now also suffixes a parameter name that appears in more than one non-body location (path, query, header, cookie). I haven't run your `id` path/query/header example against it.
- **`OpenAPIResource`:** `components.py` takes the new `arguments` keyword. `read()` builds the request with `director.build` from those arguments.
  - Client default query params and cookies are applied under the request's own values.
  - Client default headers are applied next, and incoming MCP request headers go on top.
- **`OpenAPIResourceTemplate.create_resource`:** it fills `arguments` from the route's parameter map, so suffixed names like `id__path` work. It matches template parameter names to OpenAPI names with `-` and `_` treated as the same.

Checks against a mock transport, with a client default `api-version` param and a `session` cookie:

- `resource://get_user/..%2F..%2Fadmin%2Fsecret` requested `/users/%2E%2E%2F%2E%2E%2Fadmin%2Fsecret`.
- `resource://get_user/alice?admin=true` requested `/users/alice`, with no `admin` leaking through.
- Route `/users/{user-id}` read as `resource://get_user/abc` requested `/users/abc`.

I did not exercise the body-property or query-parameter `id` collisions through a resource read.
